results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 61 aligned unit summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in the spec's order (including p26 between p23 and p24); the five callouts match no spec paragraph and are apparatus.

Introduction ¶3 (marked two_ideas): the evidence sentence and the route are one roadmap idea (what the chapter reads and in what order), exactly as p03 declares; the evidence base is part of what a roadmap predicts (AC-2).

results.quote: The 2019 revenue was €680 million across France (€357 million, mostly leboncoin), Spain (€182 million), Brazil (an equity-accounted joint venture) and a long tail of "Global Markets".
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries (central-investment commitments + revenue breakdown). p12 declares one idea, the investment backing the rule 'for a group whose' revenue was concentrated in France and Spain; the draft appends the revenue as a free-standing sentence with no link to the rule, so it reads as a second topic (flow reader A, item 4, also tripped on it).

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: phases 1–3 and the trade-offs to A1, phase 4 and failure modes to A2/A5, phase 5 to A3, reference architecture, verticals, comparison and rules to A4, how-to-read/timeline/evidence-stops to A5; the conclusion units to A1–A4.

results.quote: The 2019 revenue was €680 million across France (€357 million, mostly leboncoin), Spain (€182 million), Brazil (an equity-accounted joint venture) and a long tail of "Global Markets".
results.finding: The statistic is not followed by any sentence saying what it shows (the spec: the size and concentration of the group the rule applied to); the next paragraph turns to the rule, so the revenue figures are left unexplained.

All other evidence is explained: the timeline by Figure 1's caption; Figures 1–6 by their captions; the shared-services, layer-map, trade-off, vertical, evidence-gap, pattern and Veldmark tables by their lead-ins or the following unit (p26, p29, p59); the 2019, 2023 and 2025 quotations by p13, p32–p33 and p37–p40; the transactional table by the subheading and the inference callout after Figure 4; the coches.net example by its bold claim.

results.draft_locus: Phase 4: Verticals and the Convergence Bet (2023 to Mid-2024) ¶1
results.quote: The 2023 annual report, published in April 2024, describes the "Growing at Scale" strategy
results.finding: Declared: time, carrying over the consolidation of the uniform layers through 2023 and introducing the 2023 strategy that went further. The section opens on a new document and strategy without picking up the consolidation or saying this strategy went further (that only arrives two units later, in ¶3); after Phase 3 ends in August 2024, flow reader B (item 1) had to re-check where it was in time at this boundary.

results.quote: Under the same group strategy, Adevinta's generalist, automotive and real-estate marketplaces differed in scale, in revenue model and in which were sold or put up for sale, and so in how separable a shared capability had to be.
results.finding: Declared: elaboration carrying over the trade-offs' new condition, how long the group expects to own each tenant. The opening never names the ownership horizon or the trade-off table, so the elaboration is left for the reader to infer; both flow readers found the section's position only partly clear.

All other boundaries express their declared relationship and pick up the known information, e.g. p02 'This chapter asks three questions of each phase', p10's contrast of a spread local invention with copying, p15 'less ordinary', p18 'Regulators and strategy removed', p20/p21–p23 run-in layer heads, p26 'the only cross-marketplace product component', p25 'followed the same path', p30 'not only the components beneath it', p44 'already present', S9 'If separability can be built in', p53–p56 as parallel bold rules after 'five decision rules. The first:', p59 'The last row', p60 'The architectural answer', conclusion 'The opening's three questions'. The hand-off links [[case-olx]] (deterministic).

Both flow readers name the declared organisation: reading rules and timeline, five phases in chronological order, cross-phase views grouped (layer map to evidence gaps), then rules, comparison and questions (problem_solution); both say the roadmap matches the body and no reordering of sections is needed. Lost-thread points are recorded separately.

results.quote: The group's most durable shared abstraction was a local invention, promoted to group level.
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read to tell which 'group' is meant (Schibsted or Adevinta) and how a tool from FINN.no, which never joined Adevinta, was 'promoted'; the open-sourcing that bridges it is mentioned only in passing. The spec order is fine; the prose obscures it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 ("Which 'group' is meant?"); first reported by flow reader A, item 2

results.quote: The platform grew from about 1,500 to more than 4,000 developers, through the eCG integration, and the public record shows no mandate.
results.finding: Both readers stopped at a 2023 figure and the eCG integration inside the 2019–2020 phase, before Phase 3 introduces eCG. The spec's p16 puts the June 2023 SCHIP growth in Phase 2, so the jump comes from the declared placement; prose could at most flag it as a look-ahead.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 2 ("Phase 2 jumps ahead in time"); first reported by flow reader A, item 3

results.quote: by October 2024 it ran "over 2,000 Kubernetes nodes" in 30 clusters "across 25 marketplaces"
results.finding: The 2021–2023 phase carries October and December 2024 evidence and the August 2024 ML Golden Path, so Phase 4 (from 2023) seems to step back in time. The spec's Phase 3 heading and flow rationale keep the post-2023 consolidations here deliberately, so the difficulty comes from the declared order and heading.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, item 3 ("Phase 3's infrastructure paragraph does the same, reaching into October and December 2024"); first reported by flow reader B, item 1

results.draft_locus: Phase 4: Verticals and the Convergence Bet (2023 to Mid-2024) ¶2
results.quote: The convergence below concerns leboncoin (France) and Kleinanzeigen (European Markets), not mobile.de, and names transactions first.
results.finding: Both readers were unsure why the 2023 revenue table sits in Phase 4 until this last sentence after it. The spec's evidence says the table shows where the money came from when the convergence was decided; ¶1's lead-in could say so before the table, so the prose, not the order, obscures it.

Every does_not_know item is given at first use: Adevinta's history (introduction, timeline), SCHIP ('a multi-tenant Kubernetes distribution'), FIAAS, Houston, Fisher, YAMS ('media service'), EU5 (timeline). Other terms are in already_knows (Kubernetes, Argo CD, Kafka) or glossed (PSP, Hyrum's Law, Aurelia UK Feederco Ltd). Reader B's stops ('Cognition team', Canada, Eurek8s) are a team label, a market and a controller explained by what it does, not terms the audience needs; recorded under flow.

The introduction opens with an intriguing example (the dated pendulum), states the three questions and the thesis, and gives the evidence and route; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, dawn of man or book report.
The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', does not restate the thesis alone, add evidence or a new subtopic; the OLX question is the declared hand-off.

¶1 answers the three opening questions together, which no section does ('What it cost was set by the owner: synergy in 2021, separation in 2025'), and turns them into one rule a Chief Architect can act on (share by layer, fund convergence as its own case, design for a tenant's exit).

¶2 returns to the hook ('Adevinta shows one group running the whole pendulum in public') and ¶1 to the opening's three questions; the product layer 'is never shown finished' answers why the last swing's outcome is unknown.

The intro-only reader predicted the three questions per phase, Adevinta's reports, releases and engineering blog as evidence (strong on infrastructure/data/organization, weak on product), the thesis, the order (reading rules, timeline, five phases, cross-phase views, rules, comparison with patterns and Veldmark, questions) and an analytical, evidence-careful first-person tone; all match the roadmap.

The AC-2 reader named the three questions, the evidence (reports, releases, engineering blog, strongest on infrastructure, data and organization and weakest on core product layers), the argument (share uniform expensive layers first, treat convergence separately, design every layer so a tenant can leave) and an ending in rules, a comparison with the book's patterns and Veldmark, and questions; matches 'expected'.

The AC-1 reader sorted cloud, experimentation and image recognition as passing the 2019 two-part test with voluntary adoption; matched the merger to the 2023 'unified global platform', 'progressing well' in May 2024 and the 2025 decentralization, requiring its own investment case with scope, stage gates and exit criteria; and required tenant separability (account boundary, tenant-scoped data with contracts, portable deployment, code ownership) because a private-equity owner turns shared platforms into separation costs. Matches 'expected'.
